pageTitle: Using service-linked roles for AWS Shield network security director
whatThePageStates: This is an IAM service-linked role page for AWS Shield network security director (NSD), published inside the AWS WAF developer guide. Most of it is prose plus JSON policy snippets: what a service-linked role is, the trusted principal (network-director.amazonaws.com), the permissions the NetworkSecurityDirectorServiceLinkedRolePolicy grants (one block of actions that cannot be downscoped, then seven service-headed blocks that are downscoped to resource ARNs), and how the role is created, edited and deleted. The only genuine coverage statement is the final section, 'Supported Regions for AWS Shield network security director service-linked roles', a two-column table of 14 Regions with the sentence that NSD 'supports using service-linked roles in following regions and can only retrieve data about your resources in these regions'. Nothing on the page is a per-service or per-resource-type support matrix: the policy blocks are permission grants, not a supported/not-supported claim. The page also carries a public-preview note for NSD and a 'See also' AI-coding-assistant blurb.

features.featureName: AWS Shield network security director service-linked role Region support
features.statuses: 14 Yes, 0 No, 0 Partial; 14+0+0=14. The table has no status column at all: presence of a row is the Yes. Not-supported is not enumerated anywhere, though the lead sentence ('can only retrieve data about your resources in these regions') makes the list closed rather than illustrative, so the absent Regions are excluded by a blanket statement, not by any stated per-Region No. Rows, verbatim in page order: US East (N. Virginia) us-east-1; Europe (Stockholm) eu-north-1; Asia Pacific (Thailand) ap-southeast-7; Africa (Cape Town) ap-south-1; US East (Ohio) us-east-2; Asia Pacific (Malaysia) ap-southeast-5; Asia Pacific (Tokyo) ap-northeast-1; US West (Oregon) us-west-2; Europe (Spain) eu-south-2; Europe (Ireland) eu-west-1; Europe (Frankfurt) eu-central-1; Asia Pacific (Hong Kong) ap-east-1; Asia Pacific (Singapore) ap-southeast-1; Asia Pacific (Sydney) ap-southeast-2. Note the page itself is wrong on row 4: it pairs 'Africa (Cape Town)' with code ap-south-1 (Asia Pacific (Mumbai)) rather than af-south-1. Both columns still yield 14 distinct values, so the count is 14 either way; an auditor must not silently repair the code.
features.scope: The Region list is scoped to one thing, the service-linked role and the data NSD can retrieve through it, and it is further qualified by the note that AWS Shield network security director is in public preview and subject to change. There is no second dimension: no per-plan, per-scan-method or per-partition split. Every ARN in the policy blocks uses the aws partition only, but the page makes no partition claim.
features.reasoning: The axis is the external universe of AWS Regions, enumerated by AWS, and the unit of claim is one Region per row: each row asserts 'the NSD service-linked role works here and NSD can read your resources here'. Region name and Region code are two columns describing the same single value, not two axis values, so the row count and the target count agree and no collapse field is needed.

shouldNotExtract: The IAM policy JSON is not coverage. The first code block lists 41 actions that cannot be downscoped (2 cloudwatch, 26 ec2, 8 elasticloadbalancing, 1 wafv2, 2 cloudfront, 2 directconnect) and the seven service-headed blocks list 21 more (CloudFront 1, AWS WAF 6, AWS WAF Classic 2, AWS Direct Connect 4, AWS Transit Gateway routes 1, AWS Network Firewall 6, Amazon API Gateway 1), 62 actions in total. Those are permission grants inside a managed policy, with no Yes/No status and no assertion that a service is or is not analysed. Also not coverage: the six 'This includes' bullets, whose sixth item is literally 'And more, as detailed in the permissions list below'; the resource-ARN lists inside each Resource array; the single trusted principal bullet network-director.amazonaws.com; the create/edit/delete procedure sections; the public-preview note; the deletion-failure note; the new-console-experience banner at the top; the pointer to the 'AWS Services That Work with IAM' page and its 'Service-Linked Role' Yes column, which belongs to a different page entirely; and the 'See also' Skills-for-AI-coding-assistants boilerplate with its aws agent-toolkit search-skills command.
coverageDimensions: REGION: this page gives a closed list of 14 Regions for the NSD service-linked role, the only coverage figure it supports. SERVICE: nothing. The policy blocks name CloudFront, AWS WAF, AWS WAF Classic, Direct Connect, EC2/Transit Gateway, Network Firewall, API Gateway, CloudWatch, Elastic Load Balancing, App Runner and Cognito, but only as IAM permission targets; the page never states that a service is supported or unsupported, and the prose closes with 'And more', so any service count taken from here is fabricated. RESOURCE TYPE: nothing. ARN patterns such as arn:aws:wafv2:*:*:regional/webacl/*/* scope a permission, they are not an enumerated list of supported resource types, and there is no status against any of them. Any per-service or per-resource-type coverage number attributed to this page is invented.
trap: The single most likely misparse is treating the IAM policy blocks as a coverage matrix and harvesting either 62 API actions as an apiOperation axis or the 7 bold service headings (Amazon CloudFront, AWS WAF, AWS WAF Classic, AWS Direct Connect, AWS Transit Gateway routes, AWS Network Firewall, Amazon API Gateway) as a supported-service list. Both are permission grants, all-Yes by construction, with no stated exclusion. Runners-up: (a) reading the Region table's two columns as 28 values, or as two separate features, when name and code describe the same 14 Regions; (b) 'fixing' the page's ap-south-1 / Africa (Cape Town) mismatch and thereby recording a value the page does not state; (c) counting the six 'This includes' bullets as six capabilities when the sixth is the filler 'And more'; (d) harvesting the sentence about the 'AWS Services That Work with IAM' page and its Yes column as a status claim made by this page; (e) miscounting the ec2 actions in the first block, which is 26 long and contains several near-identical TransitGateway names; (f) treating the four bold procedure headings (Creating / Editing / Deleting / Supported Regions) as an axis.
